data.body:
Fixed and pushed: Gerrit change 2568 — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2568 (commit 03578f576442).

## The blast radius is far larger than one test, and two of them are PRODUCT regressions

Running the 31 test modules that assert on argparse help/usage text under a throwaway 3.14.7 venv produced **25 failures across 9 modules**, not the single reported one:

- tests/unit/test_advanced_cli_parsers.py — the reported test PLUS `test_build_argument_parser_accepts_presentation_passthroughs`
- tests/unit/test_cli_parser_contract.py::test_subparsers_usage_wraps_ellipsis_pre_313
- tests/interfaces/contracts/test_create_help_no_write_b8de.py — 4 tests
- tests/interfaces/contracts/test_cli_registry_distribution.py::test_clean_wheel_generators_check_clean
- tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py — 7 tests
- tests/interfaces/facades/{test_bridge_status_heldout,test_bridge_vocabulary_heldout,test_intercept_registry_cutover_s6_heldout}.py — 10 more

**Two are not brittle assertions but real user-visible defects on 3.14:**

1. `gen_cli_help.py --check` reports EVERY committed `help/*.txt` artifact stale — the byte-exact generated help would drift.
2. `RebarHelpFormatter._format_usage` wraps on rendered line LENGTH, and ANSI escapes inflate that length — so usage text would wrap differently for real users, not just in tests.

A third is a nice illustration of why this matters: `test_bridge_help_avoids_internal_vocabulary_and_numeric_exit_codes` fails because the escape sequences `\x1b[1;34m` CONTAIN DIGITS, so the 'no numeric exit codes in help' scan matches on the color codes themselves.

## Precise trigger, and why CI would not have caught it

Python 3.14 AND `_colorize.can_colorize()` true — which needs a TTY or `FORCE_COLOR` in the environment (this host sets `FORCE_COLOR=3`). Plain CI with no TTY and no FORCE_COLOR would stay green even on 3.14. So the original 'forward-looking, LOW' framing was right about CI but understated the user-facing scope.

## Fix

`src/rebar/_cli/_parser.py` — `RebarArgumentParser.__init__` sets `self.color = False` after `super().__init__`. In 3.14 `ArgumentParser._get_formatter` does `formatter._set_color(self.color)`, so that one attribute is the entire knob; subparsers are built via `parser_class` and inherit it. The attribute does not exist before 3.14, where assigning it is inert. It sits on the seam `_parser.py` already exists to hold — 'help bytes are reproducible across environments'.

REJECTED: stripping ANSI in each test — ~10 files, and it leaves both product regressions unfixed. REJECTED: a `NO_COLOR=1` autouse fixture — a new mechanism the shrink-only ratchet counts, and it would MASK the product bug rather than fix it. The chosen fix adds no mechanism at all (ratchet reports new=0).

Two regression tests added in test_cli_parser_contract.py force `FORCE_COLOR=1` and assert no `\x1b` in `format_usage()`/`format_help()`, including the subparser case; both confirmed RED without the src change.

## Results on BOTH interpreters

    3.12.13 (what CI runs)  before: green            after: 713 passed, 1 skipped
    3.14.7  (throwaway)     before: 25 failures      after: 624 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed

make lint rc 0 (complexity new=0, mechanism new=0/stale=0); make typecheck Success across 745 files.

## Deliberate follow-up, not fixed here

`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:147` builds `bridge suggest-mapping`'s parser as a bare `argparse.ArgumentParser`, outside the RebarArgumentParser family, so its help still colorizes on 3.14. No test covers it, and pulling it onto the shared factory is wider than this ticket. Worth its own ticket — it is also a latent inconsistency independent of color, since that parser misses every other RebarArgumentParser behaviour too.
